**STEP 1 - Scene:** A small serving of roasted cauliflower florets on a white square-rimmed plate, photographed from above at a near-overhead angle.

**STEP 2 - Ruler:** The plate spans roughly 26 cm across its longest undistorted width, similar to a dinner plate. Area ≈ 3.14 × (13)² ≈ 530 cm² (the rounded corners reduce this slightly, so I use about 530 cm²).

**STEP 3 - Items:** Roasted cauliflower florets with browned, slightly charred edges. A faint oil sheen is possible but not clearly visible, so I add no separate oil item.

**STEP 4 - Area:** The florets cover a loose cluster in the center-left of the plate, about 18% of the plate area (≈ 95 cm²).

**STEP 5 - Volume:** Florets are piled to about 1.5 cm on average. 95 cm² × 1.5 cm ≈ 143 ml (gross envelope).

**STEP 6 - Grams:** Cut vegetable bulk density ≈ 0.6 g/ml. 143 ml × 0.6 ≈ 86 g.

**STEP 7 - Energy:** Raw cauliflower is about 25 kcal/100 g. Roasting with a little oil raises this to roughly 35 kcal/100 g. 86 g × 0.35 ≈ 30 kcal.

**STEP 8 - Sanity check:** A plate about one-fifth covered with florets in a loose pile should hold roughly 80–90 g, so about 30 kcal is plausible. Hidden oil could add a few kcal, so the true value may be somewhat higher.

Estimated total: about 86 g and about 30 kcal.
